title: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) staging and mutual exclusivity (Stages 1–5)
text: KDIGO guidelines classify chronic kidney disease into mutually exclusive stages by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR): Stage 1 (eGFR >= 90 mL/min/1.73m2 with kidney damage), Stage 2 (eGFR 60–89), Stage 3 (eGFR 30–59), Stage 4 (eGFR 15–29), and Stage 5 (< 15 or dialysis). A patient can only be in one current CKD stage at a time; when CKD progresses (for example, from Stage 1 to Stage 2 and then Stage 3), earlier stages should be marked resolved rather than left simultaneously active on the problem list.
source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease / NIDDK
license: US Public Domain (NIDDK) / KDIGO Clinical Summary

title: Prediabetes vs. Type 2 Diabetes and Diabetic Kidney Disease progression
text: Prediabetes (HbA1c 5.7%–6.4%, SNOMED 714628002) is a precursor state before overt Type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c >= 6.5%). Once a patient develops established Type 2 diabetes complications—such as diabetic kidney disease (SNOMED 127013003), diabetic microalbuminuria (SNOMED 90781000119102), or diabetic proteinuria (SNOMED 157141000119108) requiring insulin therapy—the earlier Prediabetes entry is clinically superseded and should be reconciled as resolved.
source: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care in Diabetes / MedlinePlus

title: CDC ACIP HPV immunization schedule: 2-dose (under age 15) vs. 3-dose rule
text: CDC ACIP recommends a 2-dose HPV vaccination schedule (0 and 6–12 months) for adolescents who initiate the vaccine series before their 15th birthday (ages 9–14 years). A 3-dose schedule (0, 1–2, and 6 months) is recommended only when the series is started at age 15 years or older or for immunocompromised individuals. Administering a 3rd HPV dose (CVX 62 or 165) to an immunocompetent adolescent who received Dose 1 at age 11 is an ACIP over-immunization schedule anomaly.
source: CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) HPV Vaccine Recommendations

title: CDC ACIP Zoster (Shingles) vaccine: single-dose live Zostavax vs. 2-dose Shingrix
text: Live attenuated zoster vaccine (Zostavax, CVX 121) was a single-dose shingles vaccine that was discontinued in the United States in November 2020. Current CDC ACIP guidelines recommend 2 doses of recombinant adjuvanted zoster vaccine (Shingrix, CVX 187) spaced 2 to 6 months apart for adults aged 50 and older. Two recorded doses of live zoster vaccine (CVX 121) one year apart represent an immunization schedule or coding anomaly.
source: CDC ACIP Shingles (Herpes Zoster) Vaccination Guidelines

title: Cross-source immunization deduplication across EHRs and State Registries (WA IIS)
text: When aggregating health records from multiple sources (such as a primary care EHR, retail pharmacy, and the Washington State Immunization Information System [WA IIS]), a single vaccination event is frequently reported twice with dates differing by 1 to 2 days due to administration date vs. registry transmission/claim date. Seasonal Influenza (CVX 140) or COVID-19 mRNA (CVX 208) doses recorded within 14 days of each other across different organizations should be flagged as likely duplicate immunization records rather than separate doses.
source: CDC AIRA / HL7 FHIR Immunization Implementation Guide — Deduplication Best Practices

title: Medication reconciliation: Clopidogrel vs. Plavix brand-generic duplication
text: Clopidogrel (RxNorm 309362) and Plavix (RxNorm 213169) are the generic and brand names for the exact same P2Y12 antiplatelet ('blood thinner') medication (75 mg oral tablet). When a cardiology clinic prescribes brand Plavix while a primary care list retains generic Clopidogrel, both appear active; taking both simultaneously doubles the dose and significantly increases the risk of major gastrointestinal or intracranial bleeding.
source: DailyMed / NLM RxNorm Medication Reconciliation Guidance — Clopidogrel Bisulfate

title: Medication reconciliation: Concurrent statin therapy (Simvastatin vs. Lipitor/Atorvastatin)
text: Simvastatin (Zocor, RxNorm 312961) and Atorvastatin (Lipitor, RxNorm 617311) both belong to the HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin) class of cholesterol-lowering medications. Patients should never take two different statins at the same time; when a specialist initiates high-intensity Lipitor (atorvastatin 40 mg) after cardiac surgery, the prior Simvastatin 20 mg prescription must be discontinued to prevent severe muscle toxicity (myopathy and rhabdomyolysis) and liver injury.
source: ACC/AHA Blood Cholesterol Guideline / MedlinePlus Drug Information

title: Medication reconciliation: Lisinopril vs. Prinivil brand-generic ACE inhibitor duplication
text: Lisinopril (RxNorm 314076) and Prinivil (RxNorm 206765, also sold as Zestril) contain the same active angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor ingredient used to treat high blood pressure and protect kidney function. Concurrent active prescriptions for generic lisinopril 10 mg and brand Prinivil 10 mg across different clinics represent a brand-generic duplicate that can cause dangerous low blood pressure (hypotension), high potassium (hyperkalemia), and acute kidney injury.

title: Cross-clinic problem list reconciliation: Active vs. Resolved Chronic Sinusitis
text: In multi-source health records, a chronic condition such as Chronic sinusitis (SNOMED 40055000) may remain marked 'active' in an older primary care problem list (e.g., onset 2008) even after an ENT or specialty clinic has documented that the condition 'resolved' (e.g., abatement in 2024). Highlighting active-vs-resolved status discrepancies helps patients and clinicians clean up stale problem list entries.
source: ONC USCDI / HL7 FHIR US Core Problem List Reconciliation Guidance

title: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) hospitalization, perioperative medications, and recovery
text: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG, SNOMED 232717009 / 399261000) is open-heart surgery that routes blood around blocked coronary arteries in ischemic heart disease (SNOMED 414545008). Standard perioperative care includes intravenous cefazolin (2000 mg injection, RxNorm 1665060) for surgical site infection prophylaxis, high-dose intravenous heparin (RxNorm 1659263) during cardiopulmonary bypass reversed with protamine sulfate (RxNorm 1796676), general anesthesia (propofol, isoflurane, rocuronium, remifentanil, midazolam), ICU monitoring (arterial blood gases, troponin, coagulation panels), and a supervised walking exercise test before hospital discharge alongside long-term antiplatelet (clopidogrel), beta-blocker (metoprolol succinate), and statin therapy.
source: NHLBI / MedlinePlus — Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) Patient Guide

title: Patient privacy rights for sensitive Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) findings
text: Electronic health records often store social determinants of health (SDOH) and personal safety findings—such as 'Victim of intimate partner abuse' (SNOMED 706893006), 'Limited social contact' (SNOMED 423315002), or 'Has a criminal record' (SNOMED 266948004)—directly on the active FHIR Condition problem list alongside medical diagnoses. In a patient-facing health summary ('patient_self'), these items should be clearly flagged as privacy-sensitive so the patient knows they are recorded in the chart; when generating an external referral or school summary ('external_share'), sensitive SDOH items should be segmented and redacted unless explicitly authorized by the patient.
source: ONC Cures Act / HIPAA Privacy Rule & HL7 FHIR DS4P (Data Segmentation for Privacy)

title: Interpreting kidney function (eGFR, Creatinine) and diabetes (HbA1c) lab trajectories
text: Longitudinal kidney and metabolic health is tracked through three core blood tests: (1) Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR, LOINC 33914-3), where >= 90 mL/min/1.73m2 is normal, 60–89 is mildly reduced (Stage 2), and 30–59 indicates moderate chronic kidney disease (Stage 3); (2) Serum Creatinine (LOINC 2160-0 / 38483-4, normal ~0.7–1.3 mg/dL), which rises as kidney filtration declines; and (3) Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c, LOINC 4548-4), which measures 3-month average blood sugar (< 5.7% normal, 5.7%–6.4% prediabetes, >= 6.5% diabetes).
source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests / National Kidney Foundation Consumer Reference

title: Managing hypertension, diabetes, and coronary disease medications (Humulin 70/30, Hydrochlorothiazide, Metoprolol, Nitroglycerin)
text: In patients with combined hypertension (SNOMED 59621000), diabetic kidney disease (SNOMED 127013003), and ischemic heart disease (SNOMED 414545008): Humulin 70/30 (RxNorm 106892) provides premixed intermediate and regular insulin for glycemic control; Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg (RxNorm 310798) is a thiazide diuretic that lowers blood pressure; Metoprolol succinate 100 mg ER (RxNorm 866412) is a daily beta-blocker protecting the heart after CABG; and sublingual Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray (RxNorm 705129) is used as needed for acute chest pain.
source: MedlinePlus Drug Information — Cardiovascular & Diabetes Regimens

title: Plain-language guide to Anemia, Chronic Sinusitis, Sleep Apnea (CPAP), and Dental/Oral conditions
text: Common chronic outpatient conditions on adult problem lists include: Anemia (SNOMED 271737000, low hemoglobin/red blood cell count monitored via CBC panel LOINC 58410-2); Chronic sinusitis (SNOMED 40055000, persistent sinus inflammation); Obstructive sleep apnea (SNOMED 73430006, breathing pauses during sleep managed with a home CPAP appliance); and dental conditions including Gingivitis (SNOMED 66383009, treated with topical sodium fluoride gel RxNorm 1535362), Impacted molars (SNOMED 196416002), and Loss of teeth (SNOMED 37320007, managed with partial or complete dentures).
source: MedlinePlus Health Topics — Blood, ENT, Sleep, and Oral Health
